newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India marked lower, premiums contract.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India marked lower, premiums contract.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) fell in London as the local market dithered over its direction and all the beneficial effects of last week's cut in bank reserve requirements worked through the system.
"The rally after the credit easing was remarkably short-lived," said a trader.

The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed down 1.65 points, or 2.62 percent, at 61.52 points, with the premium over the local market at 7.55 percent, after the Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index rose 13.86 points to 3,264.52.
Premiums for GDRs declined despite a fall in the value of the Indian rupee. Usually a weaker rupee increases premiums for the dollar denominated GDRs.

"There is little appetite for taking on India in portfolios at this time, even with GDR premiums back under 10 percent. It is the story of most of this year, they are undervalued relative to the local market and in absolute terms but no-one wants it," said a trader.

The Capel Korea GDR Index lost 3.69 points, or 5.20 percent, to 67.21, a premium of 29.27 percent over the local market, after the Korea Composite Index fell 11.73 points to a provisional close of 780.08.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index closed down 0.52 points, or 0.59 percent, at 87.79, a premium of 2.18 percent after the Taiwan Weighted Index fell 34.19 points, or 0.53 percent, to 6,424.72.
